correctness.rationale: The degree-one condition forces selected components to be dominoes, and line sharing would connect two components. In the line-graph model R_{a,b}=L(K_{a,b}), selected cells correspond to edges forming vertex-disjoint two-edge paths in K_{a,b}; selected sets in a row or column are the selected edges incident to its endpoint. Two unused rows give identical signatures in a used column, two unused columns likewise, and intersecting unused lines cause non-domination. With an unused row, any horizontal domino causes a singleton signature collision with its selected mate; hence only vertical dominoes are possible. With full coverage, each unselected signature is the disjoint union of two nonempty endpoint sets and cannot equal a selected singleton. A same-line collision is impossible by disjointness of the other endpoint sets. A collision in different rows and columns would force crossed row/column sets to agree, hence each must be the singleton at the intersection, contradicting that every selected edge has an endpoint of selected degree two. With one unused row and all vertical dominoes, singleton, doubleton and triple signatures separate selected cells, unused-row cells and other cells; a triple's unique full selected column pair and its third cell recover the two coordinates. Transposition handles one unused column. The full-coverage constraints are h+2v=a and 2h+v=b. Partitioning and matching the labeled rows and columns yields a!b!/(2^(h+v)h!v!). The unused-line counts follow by reserving that line and assigning unordered pairs to the other side. The component weights XY^2/2 and X^2Y/2 give the EGF, dropping empty components as required for positive side sizes. For a=1 the rook graph is K_b: selected degree one forces two cells, and locating permits at most one unselected cell, so b=2 or 3 with counts 1 and 3. The transposed case and R_{1,1} agree, as does the square specialization.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration checks all subsets only on the stated boards, rejecting odd cardinalities by the selected-degree condition. The general classification and counts rely on the analytic proof.

evidence: The older rectangular induced-matching polynomial includes all line-disjoint domino profiles, but does not test signature injectivity. E.g. on a 3×4 board horizontal dominoes at (0,0),(0,1) and (1,2),(1,3) give the same signature {(0,0)} to (0,1) and (2,0).

Seo–Slater's criterion needs girth at least five, whereas every nondegenerate rook board has a 4-cycle or a triangle. The inspected Cappelle et al. results concern other graph classes; no exact rook result was found in those passages.
